title: Work Order (v1)
description: The architect↔worker seam, full envelope. This is the richest contract the Architect emits — the `dispatch.py --json` machine envelope: the job fields, the authorization grant, the decomposed units + staffing, the work-plan characteristics, the dispatch mode, the rendered work_order text, and the dependency edges. job-request.v1 is a strict subset / projection of this (the job fields + schema_version), so a v1 Work Order and a v1 Job Request stay one version family with no worker churn. Versioning discipline: additive fields are minor (consumers ignore unknown fields — note the permissive nested objects below, which let the Architect's internals evolve behind WorkOrder v1); breaking changes bump schema_version (major) with a compat window during which the Architect emits both.

schema_version.description: Version of the Work Order contract. Additive → minor (unknown fields ignored); breaking → bump this major + a dual-emit compat window.

body.description: Issue body — full requirements and acceptance criteria.

route.description: Model tier the Architect selected for this job.

confidence.description: Classifier confidence that this issue is implementable autonomously.

issue_url.description: Canonical URL of the issue, when known (empty string from offline fixtures).

authorization.description: The budget + scope + stop-condition grant the Architect issues for the job. Seam-stable keys are required; the Architect may add fields (consumers ignore unknown ones).

units.description: The Architect's decomposition into work units. Empty array when the job is a single undivided unit. Per-unit keys below are the seam-stable contract; the Architect may attach more.

staffing.description: How many agents staff the units and how they are assigned. Internals (complexity signals, caps) evolve behind v1; only the seam keys are required.

characteristics.description: The work-plan characteristics (strategy / purpose / issues_affected). Data-driven from app/config/workplan-rules.yml; the inner shapes evolve behind v1.

mode.description: Dispatch mode: an implementation order, or a research order on the cheap research route.

work_order.description: The fully rendered, human-readable work order text the Engineer reads.

blocked_by.description: Issues this one depends on, as {number, url} pairs (present only when the DAG was built).

blocks.description: Issues that depend on this one, as {number, url} pairs.
